definition: Offline learning is a machine learning training approach in which a model is trained on a fixed dataset that is not updated during the learning process.
details: This dataset is collected beforehand, and the learning typically occurs in a batch mode (i.e., the model is updated using batches of data, rather than a single input-output pair at a time). Once the model is trained, it can make predictions on new, unseen data. In online learning, only the set of possible elements is known, whereas in offline learning, the learner also knows the order in which they are presented.

explainer.lead: Offline learning trains a model on a fixed dataset gathered before training starts. It matters because the data never changes during learning, so what you collect upfront bounds what the model can learn.

tiers.eli5: Like studying from a printed textbook that nobody will ever revise while you read it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train in batch mode, updating the model from batches of the collected data rather than one input-output pair at a time, then deploy it to predict on unseen data. A common pitfall is assuming the fixed dataset still reflects the world once it is deployed.
tiers.paperLevel: Training occurs over a dataset fixed in advance, with batch updates rather than per-example updates. Offline learning is distinguished from online learning in that the learner knows the order in which elements are presented, not only the set of possible elements.

explainer.example: A team collects a year of sensor readings, trains a classifier on that frozen set in batches, and then applies the trained model to new readings.
